task: A Python repository's test suite is failing. Run the tests, identify the root cause in the source, fix it, and confirm the suite passes. Do not edit the tests to make them pass.
One test in this repository passes sometimes and fails other times. Determine why it is flaky, fix the underlying cause, and demonstrate the fix by running the test repeatedly.
A pull request claims a function is 2x faster after its change. Benchmark both versions on the same input and report the measured speedup. If the claim is wrong, say so and give the real number.
A project stopped building after a dependency upgrade. Find which dependency broke it and what changed, then either pin or adapt the code so the build succeeds. Show the passing build.

Count the total number of lines across all log files in a directory and write the number to a file. The usual utility for this is not installed in this environment; find another way rather than reporting failure.
A behaviour that used to work is now broken. Use the repository history to find the commit that introduced the regression, and explain what in that commit caused it.

A Triton kernel is slower than the PyTorch baseline it was meant to replace. Profile both, identify where the time goes, and report whether the kernel can be fixed or should be abandoned. Support the conclusion with measurements.
A script fails intermittently when a network call times out. Make it resilient without hiding real errors, and demonstrate the behaviour under both a failing and a succeeding call.
A service behaves differently in two environments that are supposed to be identical. Diff the effective configuration, find the divergence, and report which setting is responsible.
A function crashes on malformed input. Reproduce the crash, harden the function so it handles the bad input correctly, and add a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after.
